meta.source: Coded from the published QP and mark scheme (1MA1_3F_2506). Derived metadata only — question numbers, marks and skill tags. No exam question text transcribed.
meta.note: Marks per part read from the question paper's own part totals and checked against the printed 80. Questions 22 to 30 are the overlap questions shared with 3H (3H q1 to q8, with 3F q26 and q27 as 3H q5 and q6) and are tagged identically there.

coding_notes: q1 (place value of a digit after the decimal point) tagged decimals. The taxonomy has no place-value node; decimals is the one that claims the student can work with the decimal columns.

q2 and q10 (a square root, and a claim about a cube root) tagged indices. Roots have no node of their own and sit inside the powers-and-roots skill; indices is also the cheapest tag available, crediting only itself and simple_arithmetic.

q9b (mark the fourth vertex so the four points form a square) tagged coordinates, confirmed at review. The first pass justified this as keeping the paper off the untagged cap, which was never the reason to tag it — the cap is a guard against a paper being coded lazily, not an argument about any one item, and it has since been raised anyway. The actual justification: the grid carries labelled axes from -6 to 6 and -5 to 5 with A, B and C marked, parts (a) and (c) are coordinate work on the same grid, and the answer is a single grid position. That is honestly coordinate work, even though choosing WHICH position leans on the known properties-of-2D-shapes gap. Contrast 1F q8a, left untagged: its grid has no axes and the answer is a drawn shape. THE PRINCIPLE: tag coordinates when the deliverable is a position on a coordinate grid; leave untagged when the deliverable is a drawn shape on a bare grid.

q14b (real distance from a map) tagged ratio + measuring_lines_and_angles: unlike the 1F map-scale question, the mark scheme here awards a mark for measuring the line with a ruler, so the measurement skill is genuinely tested.

q15a (write a part of a total as a fraction) tagged fractions_of_amounts. The taxonomy's fraction nodes all describe operating ON a fraction; this is the base node and the only honest fit for forming one.
q19b (mean from a frequency table) tagged mean alone. grouped_frequency_tables would be wrong — the table is not grouped and no midpoints are involved.

q28 tagged coordinates alone. The mark scheme calls the second step 'a process to use proportion', but tagging proportion would credit the whole fractions-and-percentages chain beneath it for what is a step along a line on a grid.
